svg.text: AI-DLC in Detail — the 14 Agents & the 33 Stages
Each stage is colour-coded by its LEAD agent; support agents and conditions are listed per stage.

g.text: Requirements, user stories, scope, market research
Team formation, capacity planning, delivery sequencing
Domain design, NFRs, decomposition — broadest (10 stages)
Regulatory scanning, data classification, risk assessment
Threat modelling, security scanning, DevSecOps pipelines
Code implementation, code analysis, data modelling (3 phases)
Test strategy, test generation, performance validation
CI/CD pipelines, deployment strategy, release execution
Observability, incident response, SLO tracking, feedback loop

svg.text: Reviewers (challenge the work, never build) & the Composer

g.text: Scores task entropy, proposes a tailored EXECUTE/SKIP stage grid

svg.text: B · The 33 Stages (coloured by LEAD agent)
PHASE 1 · IDEATION — should we build it?
PHASE 2 · INCEPTION — what exactly, and in what shape?
PHASE 3 · CONSTRUCTION — build, repeated per Unit of work
PHASE 4 · OPERATION — run, observe, learn (all conditional)
Topologies: 29 inline · 2 subagent (Practices Discovery, Code Generation) · 1 pipeline (Reverse Engineering) · 1 mob (User Stories).
Construction (Phase 3) repeats its per-unit stages for every Unit of work; Build/Test and CI run once across the solution.
Source: official AWS AI-DLC docs (awslabs/aidlc-workflows). Summarized for compliance with licensing restrictions.
